neighbours.label: the number that opens a parenthetical equivalent of a preceding value: a unit conversion or alternate date in brackets ('282 THz (1064 nm)', '4.3 kPa (32 mmHg)', '61 Hijri (AD 680)')
fire: The laser emits light at 282 THz (1064 nm) in the near infrared.
The pressure fell to 4.3 kPa (32 mmHg) during the test.
The battle took place in 61 Hijri (AD 680) near the river.
The trail climbs 1,200 feet (366 meters) in the first mile.
The tank holds 50 gallons (189 liters) of fresh water.
The letter was dated 23 Shawwal 1396 (17.10.1976) by the clerk.
Bake the bread at 220 C (428 F) for about thirty minutes.
The bridge spans 4,200 feet (1,280 m) across the bay.
quiet: The laser emits light at 282 THz in the near infrared region.
The pressure fell to 4.3 kPa during the second half of the test.
The battle took place in the year 61 near the river.
The trail climbs 1,200 feet in the first mile from the lot.
The tank holds 50 gallons of fresh water for the trip.
The letter was dated in the spring of that year by the clerk.
Bake the bread at 220 C for about thirty minutes or until brown.
The bridge spans 4,200 feet across the bay to the island.

notes: Card: top examples are the first digit (or the space before it) inside a parenthesis restating a value in another unit or calendar. Near misses keep the numbers but not in a parenthetical equivalent.
